_comment: The RE-KEYED retirees of the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh. The refresh retires 87 entity keys measured against the v0.2.10 release bake (tag v0.2.10 @ 490814e). SIXTY-EIGHT of those are genuine upstream DELETIONS — the phi-3 and phi-3.5 lines, codellama, the ernie, bge and aion rows and the rest — whose artifacts left the catalog entirely. A 404 is the whole truth for them and they need no migration record. The NINETEEN rows below are the other kind: their instance ids STILL EXIST upstream, so the artifact lives on under a different key and the retired key's 404 is honest but not the whole story. Without a record, a v0.2.10 user who looks up claude-fable@5 — which held 24 instances and RESOLVED at the release — gets `entity not found` and no route to claude/fable@5, and a future change can flip any of these silently. DISCRIMINATOR, and it is measured, not asserted: for each retired key, intersect the instance ids it held at the v0.2.10 bake with the id set of the refreshed catalog. A non-empty intersection is a RE-KEY; an empty one is a deletion. BASELINE. Unlike the six curation-lever corpora beside it, this record's baseline is the PREVIOUS RELEASE, not an epoch baseline, so its keys are deliberately NOT expected in epoch_retired_keys_corpus.json and it is declared out of that reconciliation by name in epoch_retired_keys_test.go, with the reason. Each case carries the MEASURED migration record: `retired_instances` is the exact set of provider instances the key held at the v0.2.10 bake (spelled `<provider>|<model id>`), `successors` is the set of live entity keys those instances now belong to, and the optional `departed_instances` names the rows upstream removed outright. The successor set is re-derived from `retired_instances` against the live registry on every run and compared against this record, so the two cannot drift apart. Only imagen@4.0 has departed instances: three vercel imagen-4.0-*-generate-001 ids left the catalog while poe's google/imagen-4 carried the migration. See TESTING.md.

provenance.ref: the epoch-wide retired-key policy: a retired entity key is a uniform hard 404 on both seams — no alias, no redirect, no successor listing at the tool. The migration record IS the pointer, and for a RE-KEYED artifact (the id survives upstream under a different key) it is the only pointer a v0.2.10 user gets, which is why every row here names its successor.

mutation.description: vercel served Sakana's Fugu Ultra under raw_family "aura", and with no other carrier the row keyed the bare label. The refreshed catalog drops that label, so the id `sakana/fugu-ultra` is read on its own terms and the artifact keys fugu/ultra. Same row, same provider, correct lab.

This is the ONE key in this set whose looser `show` seam is not a 404: the glm FAMILY stays live with many children, so `show glm/v` answers the under-specified error rather than not-found — the same behaviour `show gpt` and `show claude` rely on, and it must never be "fixed" into a 404.
